#### Data Analysis

## Results

### Water Quality

```{r echo = FALSE}
aris_data <- read_excel("data-raw/Sacramento River ARIS Data_shared.xlsx",skip = 1) |> clean_names() |> 
  mutate(date = ymd(date))|> 
  filter(site %in% c("Rancho Caleta"))

hourly_flow_colusa <- read_csv(here("data-raw", "hourly_flow_colusa.csv"))
hourly_flow_HMC <- read_csv(here("data-raw", "hourly_discharge_HMC.csv"))
hourly_flow <- bind_rows(hourly_flow_colusa, hourly_flow_HMC)

temp_rdb <- read_csv(here("data-raw", "temp_rdb.csv"))
temp_wlk <- read_csv(here("data-raw", "temp_wlk.csv"))
daily_temp <- bind_rows(temp_rdb, temp_wlk) |> 
  mutate(temp_c = (temp-32) *5/9)
turb_rdb <- read_csv(here("data-raw", "hourly_turb_rdb.csv"))
```

```{r}
# Field days/ discrete values
dates <- aris_data |> 
  mutate(temp_u = as.numeric(daily_average_temperature_upstream_f)) |> 
  mutate(temp_d = as.numeric(daily_average_termperature_downstream_c)) |>  
  mutate(turbidity = as.numeric(ntu)) |> 
  select(date, site, flow_cfs, temp_u, temp_d, turbidity)  |> 
  distinct() 
```

#### Hydrologic Data (Flow)

These plots will more likely turn into a facet plot of 3 rows OR one plot per report with the appropriate flow station identified for each restoration site. Might also get rid of the points for the "before" if these are just from gauges and not actually collected at the site. Could just draw the full vertical line in that case for dates sampled. Same applies to WQ plots.

Do we have flow thresholds we care about here? E.g. goals for restoration project?

```{r}
#| label: fig-flow-data
#| fig-cap: "Hourly Continuous Flow Data and 'Discrete' Flow Data associated with dates of sample. Hamilton City - HMC (upstream) and USGS 11389500 - COL (downstream)"
dates <- aris_data |> 
  mutate(temp_u = as.numeric(daily_average_temperature_upstream_f)) |> 
  mutate(temp_d = as.numeric(daily_average_termperature_downstream_c)) |>  
  mutate(turbidity = as.numeric(ntu)) |> 
  select(date, site, flow_cfs, temp_u, temp_d, turbidity)  |> 
  distinct()

ggplot() + 
  geom_line(data = hourly_flow, aes(datetime, flow_cfs, color = location)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("black", "gray60"))+
  new_scale_color() + 
  geom_segment(data = dates, aes(x = date, y = -Inf, xend = date, yend = flow_cfs, color = site), linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.8) + 
  geom_point(data = dates, aes(date, flow_cfs, color = site)) + 
  labs(title = "Flow at Colusa")+
  scale_color_viridis(discrete = T, option = "turbo") + 
  theme_bw()+
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

#### Water Temperature

```{r}
#| label: fig-temperature-data
#| fig-cap: "Daily Water Temperature (C) Data Data and 'Discrete' Temperature Data associated with dates of sample. Red Bluff Diversion Dam - RDB (upstream) and Wilkins Slough - WLK (downstream)"
ggplot() +
  geom_line(data = daily_temp, aes(x = datetime, y = temp_c, color = location)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("black", "gray60"))+
  new_scale_color() + 
  geom_segment(data = dates, aes(x = date, y = -Inf, xend = date, yend = temp_u, color = site), linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.8) + 
  geom_segment(data = dates, aes(x = date, y = -Inf, xend = date, yend = temp_d, color = site), linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.8) + 
  geom_point(data = dates, aes(date, temp_u, color = site)) + 
  geom_point(data = dates, aes(date, temp_d, color = site)) + 
  labs(title = "Water Temperature Data") + 
  scale_color_viridis(discrete = T, option = "turbo") + 
  theme_bw()+
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

### ARIS

#### ARIS passage estimates

Not sure why we care about the hourly counts

```{r}
#| label: fig-aris-hourly-counts
#| fig-cap: "Average Hourly Passage in April (Rancho Caleta). Three days of sampling were conducted for each site."

aris_hourly_counts <- aris_data |> 
  group_by(site, date, hour, subsample_time_start) |> 
  reframe(subsample_total = sum(count)) |> 
  group_by(site, date, hour) |> 
  reframe(avg_count = mean(subsample_total, na.rm = TRUE),
            n = n()) |> 
  mutate(hourly_count = avg_count / (n*10) * 60 )

aris_daily_counts <- aris_hourly_counts |> 
  group_by(site, date) |> 
  reframe(daily_count = mean(hourly_count))

# aris_weekly_counts <- aris_daily_counts |> 
#   mutate(week = lubridate::week(date)) |> 
#   group_by(week, site) |> 
#   reframe(total_count = sum(daily_count)) 

aris_hourly_counts |> 
  group_by(site, hour) |> 
  reframe(avg_hourly = mean(hourly_count)) |> 
  ggplot() +
  geom_point(aes(hour, avg_hourly, color = site)) + 
  geom_line(aes(hour, avg_hourly, color = site)) + 
  # facet_wrap(~site, nrow = 3)+
  scale_color_viridis(discrete = TRUE, option = "turbo")+
  labs(title = "Hourly Fish Passage Before Restoration", y = "Hourly Fish Passage")+
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
  
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-aris-daily-passage
#| fig-cap: "Average Daily Passage in April (Rancho Caleta). Three days of sampling were conducted for each site."
# This plot will probably look like one Before and one After per site with standard deviation once we have "After" data. 

ggplot(aris_daily_counts) + 
  geom_col(aes(date,daily_count, fill = site)) + 
  facet_wrap(~site, nrow = 3)+
  scale_fill_viridis(discrete = TRUE, option = "turbo")+
  labs(title = "ARIS Daily Passage Estimate", y = "Daily Fish Passage") + 
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "top",
        axis.title.x = element_blank())
```

#### Size

Do I need to expand for total fish?

```{r}
#| label: fig-aris-size-distribution
#| fig-cap: "Size Distribution of Fish"
size_data <- aris_data |> 
  select(date, site, count, size_estimate = size_estimate_in_50mm_increments_slot_sizes_if_between_50_100_then_recorded_as_50_if_between_100_150_then_recorded_as_100_etc) |> 
  uncount(weight = count)

size_data |> 
  ggplot() + 
  geom_histogram(aes(size_estimate, fill = site), color = "black", binwidth = 50) +
  facet_wrap(~site, nrow = 3, scales = "free_y")+
  scale_fill_viridis(discrete = TRUE, option = "turbo") +
  labs(title = "Size Distribution", y = "Count", x = "Length (mm)") + 
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

#### Behavior

Do I need to expand for total fish?

```{r fig.height = 6, fig.width = 8}
#| label: fig-aris-fish-behavior
#| fig-cap: "Fish Behavior Determined from ARIS"
behavior <- aris_data |> 
  select(site, date, obs_time, behavior, count) |> 
  uncount(weight = count,.remove = FALSE) |> 
  mutate(milling = if_else(grepl("milling", behavior),1, 0),
         schooling = if_else(grepl("schooling", behavior), 1, 0),
         directional = if_else(grepl("directional", behavior), 1, 0),
         meandering = if_else(grepl("meandering", behavior), 1, 0)
  ) |> 
  select(site, date, obs_time, milling, schooling, directional, meandering) |> 
  pivot_longer(cols = milling:meandering, names_to = "behavior", values_to = "behavior_count") |> 
  group_by(date, site, behavior) |> 
  summarize(total_count = sum(behavior_count)) |> 
  ungroup()

ggplot(behavior) + geom_col(aes(date, total_count, fill = behavior)) + facet_wrap(~site, nrow = 3) +
  theme_bw()+
  theme(legend.position = "top")+
  scale_fill_viridis(discrete = TRUE)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-aris-fish-behavior-box
#| fig-cap: "Fish Behavior Boxplot determined from ARIS"
ggplot(behavior) + 
  geom_boxplot(aes(site, total_count, fill = behavior), 
               position = position_dodge()) +
  scale_fill_viridis(discrete = TRUE)+
  theme_bw()+
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```
